definition: to act first in order to prevent something or to take its place

examples.text: The general attacked at dawn to preempt an enemy advance.
A quick dose of the vaccine can preempt an outbreak.
I preempted my mom's question by announcing that my homework was done.

confused.note: To preempt is to act first to block something; to prompt is to cause or remind.

questions.passage: Knowing that critics would attack the report's small sample size, the authors sought to ______ the objection. Their opening paragraph acknowledges the limitation and explains why the findings still deserve attention.
questions.explanation: Addressing the objection before it is raised acts first to head it off.

distractors.why: Deplore means to condemn strongly, which is not what the authors do to the objection.
Vilify means to speak of as evil, which does not fit.
Burgeon means to grow rapidly, and it cannot take an object.

partsNote: from Latin emere, "to buy": to buy before others can

definition: to say or write very unpleasant things about someone so that others think badly of them

examples.text: Newspapers loyal to the king vilified the reformers as traitors.
The villagers vilify the old woman as a witch until she saves a drowning child.
Fans vilified the referee online for a week after the final.

confused.note: To vilify is to slander; to verify is to confirm.

questions.passage: During her lifetime the scientist was ______ by rivals who called her methods careless and her conclusions absurd. Only after her death was her work recognized as decades ahead of its time.
questions.explanation: Being called careless and absurd by rivals is being spoken of harshly.

distractors.why: Rebuked means scolded sharply for a fault; sustained public attacks on her reputation are vilification.
Preempted means forestalled, which does not fit.
Circumvented means got around, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin vilis, "cheap, worthless": to make vile

definition: to feel or express strong disapproval of something

examples.text: The bishop deplored the violence but refused to name those responsible.
The narrator deplores his own cowardice on every page.
My grandmother deplores the way people text at the dinner table.

confused.note: To deplore is to condemn or regret; to explore is to investigate.

questions.passage: The editorial does not merely disagree with the decision to close the public library. It ______ the move, calling it "a shameful abandonment of the city's children."
questions.explanation: "Shameful abandonment" expresses strong disapproval.

distractors.why: Preempts means forestalls, which does not fit.
Circumvents means gets around, which does not fit.
Permeates means spreads through, which does not fit.

definition: able or likely to change

examples.text: Viruses with mutable genes can quickly evade a vaccine.
The poem compares human loyalty to the mutable moon.
Our weekend plans are mutable until someone checks the weather.

confused.note: Mutable means changeable; mutual means shared by two or more.

questions.passage: Spelling in the 1500s was highly ______. The same writer might spell a word three different ways on a single page, and no dictionary yet existed to say which was correct.
questions.explanation: Spelling that varied even within one page was changeable.

distractors.why: Germane means relevant, which does not describe spelling.
Noxious means harmful, which does not fit.
Consummate means supremely skilled, which does not fit.

definition: connected with and important to the subject being discussed

examples.text: The judge ruled that the defendant's childhood was not germane to the case.
Only two of the forty studies were germane to the question.
Your point about lunch is not germane to a discussion of the science fair.

confused.note: Germane means relevant; it has no connection to Germany.

questions.passage: The chair asked speakers to confine themselves to ______ remarks. A meeting called to discuss the new bus routes, she said, was not the place for complaints about the mayor's haircut.
questions.explanation: Remarks about bus routes are relevant to the meeting's subject.

distractors.why: Ludicrous means ridiculous, which the chair would not request.
Boisterous means noisy, which is not what she asks for.
Quaint means charmingly old-fashioned, which does not fit.

definition: to grow or develop quickly

examples.text: Algae burgeon in the lake each summer when the water warms.
The town burgeoned after the railway arrived.
My sister's collection of houseplants has burgeoned into a small jungle.

confused.note: To burgeon is to grow fast; to bludgeon is to beat with a heavy object.

questions.passage: Ten years ago the neighborhood had a single café. Since then the restaurant scene has ______: more than sixty new places have opened, and visitors now travel across the city to eat there.
questions.explanation: Growing from one café to more than sixty is rapid growth.

distractors.why: Languished means declined or stayed neglected, the opposite of this growth.
Meandered means wandered, which does not fit.
Capitulated means surrendered, which does not fit.

definition: the main character in a story; a leading figure in a real event

examples.text: The novel's protagonist is a lighthouse keeper who has not spoken in a year.
She was a protagonist in the struggle for voting rights.
In my little brother's stories, the protagonist is always a dinosaur.

confused.note: The protagonist is the main character; the antagonist opposes him or her.

questions.passage: Unusually for a detective novel, the ______ is not the investigator but the thief. Readers follow her through every chapter and, by the end, find themselves hoping that she will escape.
questions.explanation: The character readers follow throughout is the main character.

distractors.why: An archetype is a typical model or pattern, not the central character of a particular book.
An arbiter is a judge, which does not fit.
An insurgent is a rebel, which does not fit.

definition: done openly and without shame, said of something bad

examples.text: The election was marked by blatant fraud at the polling stations.
The courtier's blatant flattery embarrasses even the king.
Copying my answer and my spelling mistake was a blatant giveaway.

confused.note: Blatant means glaringly obvious; latent means hidden.

questions.passage: The review accused the author of ______ plagiarism. Entire paragraphs, it showed, had been lifted word for word from a well-known textbook, with not even the examples changed.
questions.explanation: Copying whole paragraphs word for word is open and obvious.

distractors.why: Subtle means hard to detect, the opposite of copying entire paragraphs.
Unwitting means unintentional; the review's point is how obvious the copying was.
Quaint means charmingly old-fashioned, which does not fit.

definition: secret cooperation between people in order to do something dishonest

examples.text: The inquiry found collusion between the customs officers and the smugglers.
The journal investigated possible collusion between reviewers and authors.
I suspect collusion between my siblings over who gets the last slice.

confused.note: Collusion is secret cooperation in wrongdoing; a collision is a crash.

questions.passage: The three companies claimed to be fierce competitors. Investigators found evidence of ______, however: for years their executives had met in secret to agree on the prices each would charge.
questions.explanation: Secretly agreeing on prices is dishonest cooperation.

distractors.why: A respite is a short rest, which does not fit.
An inclination is a tendency, which does not describe a secret agreement.
A synthesis is a combination of ideas, which does not fit.

definition: a feeling that makes you want to do something; a tendency

examples.text: The heroine's first inclination is to burn the letter unread.
The young king showed little inclination to govern.
I have no inclination to go running in the rain.

confused.note: An inclination is a leaning or tendency; an incline is a slope.

questions.passage: Although her training was in chemistry, the young scientist's natural ______ was toward biology. She spent her free hours watching birds and eventually changed fields entirely.
questions.explanation: Being drawn toward biology is a natural leaning.

distractors.why: Collusion is secret cooperation in wrongdoing, which does not fit.
A respite is a break, which does not fit.
An archetype is a typical model, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin clinare, "to lean": leaning toward

definition: so foolish or unreasonable that it is laughable

examples.text: The claim that the tiny island could conquer the continent was ludicrous.
The duke appears in a ludicrous hat the size of a cartwheel.
It is ludicrous to pay twelve dollars for a bottle of water.

confused.note: Ludicrous means ridiculous; lucrative means profitable.

questions.passage: The idea that a person could walk from one coast to the other in a week is ______. The distance is nearly five thousand kilometers, which would require covering seven hundred kilometers a day.
questions.explanation: A claim that requires an impossible daily distance is laughably unreasonable.

distractors.why: Tenable means defensible, the opposite of an impossible claim.
Pensive means thoughtful, which does not describe an idea.
Germane means relevant, which is not the issue.

definition: failing to take proper care in doing something

examples.text: The inquiry found the harbor master negligent in failing to light the beacon.
A negligent technician left the samples unrefrigerated overnight.
I was negligent about watering the plants, and they showed it.

confused.note: Negligent means careless; negligible means too small to matter.

questions.passage: The court ruled that the landlord had been ______. Tenants had reported the broken stair rail four times in writing, and he had done nothing before the fall that injured a child.
questions.explanation: Ignoring four written reports of a hazard is failing to take proper care.

distractors.why: Vigilant means watchful, the opposite of ignoring warnings.
Negligible means too small to matter; it looks similar but does not mean careless.
Indignant means angry at unfairness, which does not describe the landlord's failure.

definition: attractive because it is unusual and old-fashioned

examples.text: The story is set in a quaint fishing village of crooked lanes.
Visitors found the old custom of bowing to the clock tower quaint.
My grandparents still use a quaint rotary phone.

confused.note: Quaint means charmingly old-fashioned; to acquaint is to make familiar.

questions.passage: Tourists adore the town's ______ main street. Its shops still have hand-painted signs, a horse trough stands outside the bank, and the single traffic light was installed only last year.
questions.explanation: Hand-painted signs and a horse trough are charmingly old-fashioned.

distractors.why: Noxious means harmful, which tourists would not adore.
Blatant means glaringly obvious wrongdoing, which does not fit.
Nomadic means wandering, which does not describe a street.

definition: a short period of rest or relief from something difficult

examples.text: A week of fog gave the besieged city a respite from the cannon.
The cool spell offered a brief respite from the drought.
Lunch is my only respite on days with six classes.

confused.note: A respite is a break; despite means in spite of.

questions.passage: For the nurses, who had worked double shifts for a month, the holiday weekend brought a welcome ______. For three days the ward was quiet, and several of them slept for the first time in weeks.
questions.explanation: Three quiet days after a month of double shifts is a rest from hardship.

distractors.why: Collusion is secret cooperation, which does not fit.
A synthesis is a combination, which does not fit.
A boon is a benefit; the sentence stresses relief and rest, which is a respite.

definition: to find a way around a rule, problem, or obstacle

examples.text: Merchants circumvented the embargo by shipping goods through a neutral port.
The new technique circumvents the need for surgery.
I circumvented the website's block by using the library computer.

confused.note: To circumvent is to get around; circumspect means cautious.

questions.passage: The law limited each family to one fishing license. Some ______ it by registering additional licenses in the names of cousins, grandparents, and, in one case, a household's dog.
questions.explanation: Registering licenses under other names gets around the limit.

distractors.why: Deplored means condemned, which is not what these families did.
Preempted means acted first to prevent; the families found a way around an existing law.
Permeated means spread through, which does not fit.

definition: very common, said of something bad; full of

examples.text: The port was rife with smugglers and spies.
Disease was rife in the crowded camps.
The comment section is rife with spelling mistakes.

confused.note: Rife means widespread, usually of something bad; ripe means ready to eat or ready to happen.

questions.passage: In the months before the election, the capital was ______ with rumors. Every café had its own account of secret alliances, forged ballots, and generals who were said to be plotting a coup.
questions.explanation: A city where every café has its own rumors is full of them.

distractors.why: Germane means relevant, and "germane with rumors" is not idiomatic.
Meager means scanty, the opposite of being full of rumors.
Mutable means changeable, which does not fit "with rumors."

definition: moving from place to place without a permanent home

examples.text: Nomadic herders followed the grass across the steppe each season.
The species is nomadic, ranging hundreds of miles in search of fruit.
My aunt lives a nomadic life, working from a different country every few months.

confused.note: Nomadic means wandering; monastic relates to monks and monasteries.

questions.passage: The people of the high plateau are traditionally ______. They own no land and build no permanent houses, moving their tents and herds every few weeks to wherever the grazing is best.
questions.explanation: Moving tents and herds every few weeks is living without a permanent home.

distractors.why: Sedentary means settled in one place, the opposite of this life.
Boisterous means noisy and lively, which is not described.
Apathetic means lacking interest, which does not fit.

definition: to speak severely to someone because they have done something wrong

examples.text: The queen rebuked her ministers for hiding the news of the defeat.
The captain rebukes the boy for sleeping on watch.
The librarian rebuked us for eating chips near the computers.

confused.note: To rebuke is to scold; to rebut is to argue against.

questions.passage: The judge did not fine the lawyer, but she did ______ him sharply. Arriving an hour late without explanation, she told him before the whole court, showed contempt for everyone whose time he had wasted.
questions.explanation: A sharp public scolding for lateness is a rebuke.

distractors.why: Vilify means to slander someone's character, which goes far beyond a sharp scolding.
Circumvent means to get around, which does not fit.
Preempt means to forestall, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Old French bucher, "to beat": to beat back

definition: very small in amount; not enough

examples.text: The soldiers survived the winter on meager rations of bread and onions.
The expedition's meager data could not settle the question.
My meager savings will not cover a new phone.

confused.note: Meager means scanty; eager means enthusiastic.

questions.passage: The museum's budget is ______. It cannot afford a full-time guard, heats only two of its eight rooms in winter, and relies on volunteers to sell tickets.
questions.explanation: A budget that cannot cover guards or heat is very small.

distractors.why: Rife means widespread, which does not describe a budget.
Consummate means supremely skilled or complete, which does not fit.
Ludicrous means laughably absurd; the details show the budget is small, not absurd.

definition: showing great skill; complete or perfect

examples.text: A consummate diplomat, she ended the war without firing a shot.
The actor gives a consummate performance as the aging king.
My uncle is a consummate storyteller who can hold a room for an hour.

confused.note: Consummate means supremely skilled or complete; to consume is to use up or eat.

questions.passage: The pianist was a ______ professional. When a string snapped in the middle of the concerto, she shifted the passage to a different octave without missing a beat, and most of the audience never knew.
questions.explanation: Recovering so smoothly that no one noticed shows supreme skill.

distractors.why: Negligent means careless, the opposite of her skill.
Indignant means angry at unfair treatment, which is not shown.
Nomadic means wandering, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin summa, "sum, highest": brought to the highest point

definition: a perfect or typical example of something; an original model

examples.text: The wise old mentor is an archetype found in stories from every culture.
The city's forum became the archetype for town squares across the empire.
With his clipboard and whistle, our coach is the archetype of a gym teacher.

confused.note: An archetype is an original model or universal pattern; a stereotype is an oversimplified image of a group.

questions.passage: The reluctant hero who refuses the call to adventure and then accepts it is an ______. Versions of the figure appear in ancient epics, medieval romances, and nearly every modern blockbuster.
questions.explanation: A figure that recurs across ages and cultures is a universal pattern.

distractors.why: A protagonist is the main character of one story; a pattern found in many stories is an archetype.
A respite is a break, which does not fit.
Collusion is secret cooperation, which does not fit.

definition: poisonous or very harmful

examples.text: The factory released noxious gases that killed fish for miles downstream.
Miners carried canaries to warn them of noxious air.
The noxious smell from the gym bag suggested it had not been opened in weeks.

confused.note: Noxious means poisonous or harmful; obnoxious means extremely unpleasant or annoying.

questions.passage: Firefighters ordered everyone within a kilometer of the warehouse to leave their homes. The burning chemicals were producing ______ fumes, and several people nearby had already been taken to the hospital.
questions.explanation: Fumes that sent people to the hospital are poisonous.

distractors.why: Quaint means charmingly old-fashioned, which does not fit.
Meager means scanty, which is not why people were evacuated.
Mutable means changeable, which is not the danger.

definition: noisy, energetic, and cheerful

examples.text: A boisterous wedding party spills out of the inn and into the square.
The boisterous crowd carried the champion through the streets.
My boisterous cousins turn every dinner into a shouting match about nothing.

confused.note: Boisterous means noisy and lively; boastful means bragging.

questions.passage: The library's reading room is silent, but the children's section next door is another matter. On Saturday mornings it fills with ______ six-year-olds who shout, sing, and stage sword fights with rolled-up posters.
questions.explanation: Shouting, singing, and mock sword fights are noisy and energetic.

distractors.why: Pensive means quietly thoughtful, the opposite of these children.
Apathetic means lacking energy or interest, which they are not.
Negligent means careless, which is not the quality described.

definition: angry because of something that seems unfair or wrong

examples.text: Indignant farmers marched on the capital to protest the grain tax.
She gives an indignant reply to the suggestion that she cheated.
My brother was indignant when I got the larger slice.

confused.note: Indignant means angry at unfairness; indigent means very poor.

questions.passage: Customers were ______ when they learned that the airline had sold more tickets than there were seats. Several refused to leave the gate, insisting loudly that they had paid for a place and were entitled to it.
questions.explanation: Refusing to leave and insisting on their rights shows anger at unfair treatment.

distractors.why: Apathetic means not caring, the opposite of their reaction.
Quaint means charmingly old-fashioned, which does not fit.
Germane means relevant, which does not describe customers.

partsNote: from Latin dignus, "worthy": treating as unworthy

definition: showing no interest, enthusiasm, or concern

examples.text: An apathetic public barely noticed the change of government.
The apathetic clerk stamps each form without reading it.
I was apathetic about the election until I learned what was on the ballot.

confused.note: Apathetic means lacking interest; pathetic means causing pity or contempt.

questions.passage: Organizers had hoped that the proposal to rebuild the playground would stir strong feelings. Instead residents seemed ______: only nine people attended the meeting, and none of them stayed for the vote.
questions.explanation: Low attendance and leaving before the vote show a lack of interest.

distractors.why: Indignant means angry, which would have brought a crowd.
Boisterous means noisy and energetic, the opposite of this response.
Consummate means supremely skilled, which does not fit.

definition: aware of something; having knowledge of it

examples.text: The council was fully cognizant of the risks when it opened the port.
Researchers must be cognizant of how their presence changes animal behavior.
I am cognizant of the fact that the dishes will not wash themselves.

confused.note: Cognizant means aware; cognitive relates to thinking and mental processes.

questions.passage: The board insists that it was fully ______ of the dangers. Minutes of its meetings show that members discussed the possibility of a leak on at least six occasions before approving the pipeline.
questions.explanation: Discussing the danger six times shows the board was aware of it.

distractors.why: Unwitting means unaware, the opposite of what the minutes show.
Vacuous means empty-headed, and "vacuous of the dangers" is not idiomatic.
Contingent means dependent on something else, which does not fit.

definition: expressing disapproval or contempt, said of a word or remark

examples.text: "Carpetbagger" began as a pejorative term for northerners who moved south after the war.
The critic uses "sentimental" in a pejorative sense.
"Nerd" used to be pejorative, but my friends wear it proudly.

confused.note: Pejorative means disparaging; a prerogative is a special right.

questions.passage: The word "amateur" simply means someone who does a thing for love, not money. In everyday speech, however, it has acquired a ______ sense, suggesting work that is clumsy or second-rate.
questions.explanation: A sense suggesting clumsy work expresses disapproval.

distractors.why: Therapeutic means healing, which does not describe a word's sense.
Terrestrial means of the land or Earth, which does not fit.
Tenable means defensible, which does not fit.

definition: belonging to a different time, so seeming out of place

examples.text: The film's anachronistic wristwatch on a Roman soldier amused the audience.
The cavalry charge was already anachronistic in an age of machine guns.
Paying by check feels anachronistic when everyone else taps a phone.

confused.note: Anachronistic means out of its proper time; anarchistic means opposed to all government.

questions.passage: Historians praised the film's costumes but complained about one ______ detail. In a scene set in 1650, a character glances at a pocket watch of a design not invented until two centuries later.
questions.explanation: An object from a later century is out of place in time.

distractors.why: Pejorative means disparaging, which does not describe a watch.
Intermittent means stopping and starting, which does not fit.
Sardonic means mocking, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Greek ana, "against": against the time

definition: not aware of what is really happening; not intended

examples.text: The courier was an unwitting carrier of secret messages sewn into his coat.
Travelers became unwitting carriers of the seeds on their shoes.
I was an unwitting accomplice in my brother's plan to hide the vegetables.

confused.note: Unwitting means unaware; unwilling means reluctant.

questions.passage: The tourists had no idea that the small carved figures they bought were stolen. They became ______ participants in a smuggling ring, carrying the pieces through customs in their own luggage.
questions.explanation: Taking part without knowing it is being unaware of what is happening.

distractors.why: Cognizant means aware, but they had no idea.
Vociferous means loud and insistent, which does not fit.
Ironic describes a twist of expectation, not the tourists' lack of knowledge.

definition: thinking deeply, especially in a quiet or sad way

examples.text: The heroine sits pensive at the window while the party goes on below.
A pensive portrait shows the president a week before the war began.
My usually chatty friend was pensive on the bus ride home.

confused.note: Pensive means deep in thought; it is unrelated to cost.

questions.passage: After the letter arrived, the usually talkative professor grew ______. He stood for a long time at the window, turning the envelope over in his hands, and did not seem to hear when students greeted him.
questions.explanation: Standing silently, lost in thought, shows deep, quiet reflection.

distractors.why: Vociferous means loud and outspoken, the opposite of his silence.
Sardonic means mocking, which is not what the scene shows.
Vacuous means empty of thought, the opposite of someone thinking deeply.

definition: to spread through every part of something

examples.text: Water slowly permeates the porous rock.
A spirit of reform permeated the new parliament.
The smell of garlic permeated the whole apartment.

confused.note: To permeate is to spread through; to permit is to allow.

questions.passage: The founder's belief in thrift came to ______ the whole company. Decades after her death, executives still flew in the cheapest seats, and no office, however senior its occupant, had a carpet.
questions.explanation: A belief that shapes behavior at every level has spread through the company.

distractors.why: Circumvent means to get around, which does not fit.
Preempt means to forestall, which does not fit.
Aggregate means to collect into a whole, which does not fit a belief and a company.

partsNote: from Latin meare, "to pass": to pass through

definition: showing that you think you are better than others by mocking them; grimly humorous

examples.text: The butler's sardonic "Very good, sir" makes the insult plain.
The general's sardonic telegram read, "Reinforcements welcome, if not too much trouble."
My sister greeted my new haircut with a sardonic "Bold choice."

confused.note: Sardonic means mockingly cynical; it has nothing to do with fish.

questions.passage: Asked whether she was pleased with the committee's decision to study the problem for another year, the scientist gave a ______ smile. "Delighted," she said. "The glacier will be so grateful for the extra time."
questions.explanation: Her remark is mocking, saying the opposite of what she means.

distractors.why: Pensive means quietly thoughtful, which does not capture her mockery.
Indignant means openly angry; she expresses her displeasure through dry mockery.
Therapeutic means healing, which does not fit.

definition: showing no intelligence, thought, or purpose; empty

examples.text: The villain's nephew wears a vacuous grin through every scene.
The treaty's vacuous promises of friendship changed nothing.
The talk show was an hour of vacuous chatter about celebrity pets.

confused.note: Vacuous means empty-headed; vicious means cruel.

questions.passage: Reviewers agreed that the film was beautiful to look at and ______ in every other respect. Its characters said nothing worth hearing, and its plot seemed to have been assembled from the trailers of better movies.
questions.explanation: A film with nothing worth hearing is empty of thought.

distractors.why: Tenable means defensible, which does not describe a film.
Cognizant means aware, which does not fit.
Circuitous means roundabout, which is not the complaint.

definition: expressing opinions loudly and forcefully

examples.text: Vociferous crowds outside the palace demanded the minister's resignation.
The innkeeper is vociferous in his complaints about the new road.
My little brother is vociferous about his right to the window seat.

confused.note: Vociferous means loud and insistent; voracious means extremely hungry.

questions.passage: The plan to cut the bus route had few supporters and many ______ opponents. Hundreds of them filled the council chamber, chanting so loudly that the meeting had to be suspended.
questions.explanation: Opponents who chant loudly enough to stop a meeting are loud and forceful.

distractors.why: Apathetic means uninterested, the opposite of these protesters.
Unwitting means unaware, which does not describe deliberate protest.
Pensive means quietly thoughtful, the opposite of chanting.

definition: longer than the most direct way; roundabout

examples.text: The army took a circuitous route through the hills to avoid the fort.
By a circuitous path of hints and questions, the lawyer reaches the truth.
We took a circuitous way home to avoid the traffic and added an hour.

confused.note: Circuitous means roundabout; circular means shaped like a circle or going in a loop.

questions.passage: The trail to the lake is ______. Although the water lies only a kilometer from the parking lot, the path loops around a marsh, climbs a ridge, and doubles back twice, covering nearly five kilometers.
questions.explanation: A five-kilometer path to a point one kilometer away is roundabout.

distractors.why: Terrestrial means on land, which is not the point.
Intermittent means stopping and starting, which does not describe a route's shape.
Superficial means shallow, which does not fit.

definition: able to be defended against attack or criticism

examples.text: Once the fossils were dated, the old theory was no longer tenable.
With its water supply cut, the fort's position was not tenable.
"The dog ate it" is not a tenable excuse when you do not own a dog.

confused.note: Tenable means defensible; tenuous means weak or thin.

questions.passage: For years the company maintained that its product was harmless. That claim ceased to be ______ when its own internal studies, showing clear evidence of harm, were made public.
questions.explanation: A claim contradicted by the company's own studies can no longer be defended.

distractors.why: Tenuous means weak; "ceased to be tenuous" would mean the claim grew stronger.
Pejorative means disparaging, which does not describe a claim's defensibility.
Irrational means unreasonable; the claim became less reasonable, not less irrational.

definition: to make a problem or difficulty worse by adding to it

examples.text: The king compounded his error by refusing to apologize.
Drought compounded the damage done by the insects.
I compounded my lateness by forgetting the tickets.

confused.note: To compound is to make worse or to combine; to confound is to confuse.

questions.passage: The team's troubles began when its best player was injured. They were ______ a week later, when the coach resigned and two more starters left for rival clubs.
questions.explanation: Further losses added to the existing trouble and made it worse.

distractors.why: Alleviated means eased, the opposite of what happened.
Manifested means showed clearly; the sentence describes troubles growing worse.
Aggregated means gathered into a total, which does not convey worsening.

definition: a total formed by adding several amounts or things together

examples.text: The aggregate of the five samples weighed just under a gram.
In the aggregate, the small donations exceeded the gifts of the wealthy.
The aggregate of my quiz scores was better than I expected.

confused.note: An aggregate is a total; to aggravate is to make worse.

questions.passage: No single change in the recipe made much difference. In the ______, however, the dozen small adjustments, a little less salt here, a slightly cooler oven there, transformed the bread.
questions.explanation: Many small changes taken together form a total effect.

distractors.why: A synthesis is a blending of ideas into something new; the fixed phrase for "taken all together" is "in the aggregate."
A boon is a benefit, which does not fit "in the."
An archetype is a model, which does not fit.

definition: to come out into view; to become known

examples.text: The cicadas emerge from the ground once every seventeen years.
A new merchant class emerged in the towns along the river.
My brother emerged from his room at noon, blinking.

confused.note: To emerge is to come out; to immerse is to plunge in.

questions.passage: At first the survey's results looked random. Only when the answers were sorted by age did a pattern ______: respondents under thirty overwhelmingly preferred one option, and those over sixty the other.
questions.explanation: A pattern that becomes visible after sorting comes into view.

distractors.why: Permeate means to spread through something and needs an object.
Aspire means to hope to achieve, which a pattern cannot do.
Compound means to worsen or combine, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin mergere, "to dip": to come out of the water

definition: helping to heal or to make someone feel better

examples.text: The plant's therapeutic properties were known long before chemists isolated the drug.
Hot springs were prized for their therapeutic waters.
I find chopping vegetables oddly therapeutic after a stressful day.

confused.note: Therapeutic means healing; theoretical means based on theory.

questions.passage: Hospitals have begun to recognize the ______ value of gardens. Patients whose rooms overlook trees, studies show, need less pain medication and go home sooner than those who face a brick wall.
questions.explanation: Less pain medication and faster recovery show a healing effect.

distractors.why: Pejorative means disparaging, which does not fit.
Superficial means shallow or slight, but the benefit is real and measurable.
Terrestrial means of the land, which is not the point.

definition: the combining of separate ideas or things into a connected whole

examples.text: The paper offers a synthesis of thirty years of research on sleep.
Her style is a synthesis of folk tale and science fiction.
Our group presentation was a synthesis of four very different drafts.

confused.note: Synthesis puts parts together; analysis takes a whole apart.

questions.passage: The architect's design is neither purely traditional nor purely modern. It is a ______ of the two, setting a steel and glass tower on a base of hand-cut local stone.
questions.explanation: Combining two styles into one design is a blending into a whole.

distractors.why: An aggregate is a sum of separate items; a design that fuses two styles into something new is a synthesis.
A respite is a break, which does not fit.
Collusion is secret cooperation in wrongdoing, which does not fit.

definition: happening in the opposite way to what is expected, often in an amusing way; saying the opposite of what is meant

examples.text: It is ironic that the miser dies while counting money he will never spend.
It is ironic that the "unsinkable" ship sank on its first voyage.
It was ironic that the fire station burned down.

confused.note: Ironic means contrary to expectation; iconic means widely recognized as a symbol.

questions.passage: It is ______ that the man who invented the traffic light was killed in a collision at an intersection. He had devoted his career to preventing exactly that kind of accident.
questions.explanation: The outcome is the opposite of what his life's work would lead one to expect.

distractors.why: Therapeutic means healing, which does not fit.
Tenable means defensible, which does not describe an event.
Intermittent means off and on, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Greek eiron, "one who pretends ignorance"

definition: depending on something else that may or may not happen

examples.text: The plant's flowering is contingent on at least six weeks of cold.
The alliance was contingent on the king's marriage to the duke's daughter.
The beach trip is contingent on finishing our chores by noon.

confused.note: Contingent means dependent on something; a continent is a large landmass.

questions.passage: The grant is not guaranteed for all five years. Funding after the second year is ______ on the laboratory's showing that at least one of its three vaccines is safe for human trials.
questions.explanation: Funding that depends on a condition being met is contingent.

distractors.why: Cognizant means aware, which does not fit funding.
Manifest means obvious, which does not fit "on the laboratory's showing."
Superficial means shallow, which does not fit.

definition: easy to see or understand; obvious

examples.text: The general's manifest reluctance to attack cost him his command.
The drug's benefits were manifest within a week.
Her relief at finishing the test was manifest.

confused.note: Manifest means obvious; a manifesto is a public declaration of aims.

questions.passage: The witness tried to appear calm, but her nervousness was ______. Her voice shook, she twisted a handkerchief in her lap, and she twice asked for the question to be repeated.
questions.explanation: A shaking voice and fidgeting make her nervousness obvious.

distractors.why: Latent means hidden, but her nervousness showed plainly.
Contingent means dependent on something, which does not fit.
Anachronistic means out of its time, which does not fit.

definition: not based on reason or clear thinking

examples.text: Fear of flying is irrational, given how much more dangerous driving is.
The market's irrational panic wiped out fortunes in a single afternoon.
My irrational dislike of the color orange has no explanation.

confused.note: Irrational means not reasonable; irritable means easily annoyed.

questions.passage: The investor knew that his attachment to the failing company was ______. Every analysis told him to sell, yet he held on because his grandfather had once worked in its factory.
questions.explanation: Ignoring every analysis for a sentimental reason is not based on clear thinking.

distractors.why: Tenable means defensible, but he knew his choice was not.
Vociferous means loud, which does not describe an attachment.
Manifest means obvious, which is not what he recognized about his attachment.

definition: concerned only with what is obvious; not deep or thorough

examples.text: The cut was superficial and needed only a bandage.
Beneath their superficial politeness, the sisters are at war.
A superficial reading of the contract missed the fee on page nine.

confused.note: Superficial means shallow; superfluous means more than needed.

questions.passage: The resemblance between the two paintings is only ______. Both show a woman at a window, but a closer look reveals entirely different techniques, colors, and attitudes toward the subject.
questions.explanation: A resemblance that disappears on closer inspection lies only on the surface.

distractors.why: Profound means deep, the opposite of a likeness that vanishes on inspection.
Contingent means dependent, which does not fit.
Ironic means contrary to expectation, which is not the point.

definition: relating to the Earth or to land, as opposed to the sea or sky

examples.text: Frogs begin life in water and become terrestrial as adults.
The treaty covered terrestrial borders but said nothing about the sea.
I prefer terrestrial hobbies; boats make me queasy.

confused.note: Terrestrial relates to the Earth or land; celestial relates to the sky or heavens.

questions.passage: Whales are descended from ______ ancestors. Fossils show that fifty million years ago, their forebears were four-legged mammals that hunted along riverbanks before taking permanently to the sea.
questions.explanation: Four-legged mammals on riverbanks lived on land.

distractors.why: Aquatic means living in water, which describes whales now, not their ancestors.
Intermittent means off and on, which does not fit.
Sardonic means mocking, which does not fit.

definition: to have a strong desire to achieve something

examples.text: The young clerk aspired to a seat in parliament.
The heroine aspires to something larger than her village can offer.
I aspire to make a pancake as round as my grandmother's.

confused.note: To aspire is to aim for something; to inspire is to fill someone with the urge to do something.

questions.passage: From the age of seven, when she first watched a rocket launch on television, Okafor ______ to become an astronaut. She studied physics, learned to fly, and applied to the space program four times before she was accepted.
questions.explanation: Years of preparation toward a goal show a strong desire to achieve it.

distractors.why: Emerged means came into view, which does not fit "to become an astronaut."
Permeated means spread through, which does not fit.
Compounded means made worse, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin spirare, "to breathe": to breathe toward

definition: something very helpful that improves your life

examples.text: The canal was a boon to farmers who could now ship grain cheaply.
The new telescope has been a boon to astronomers studying distant galaxies.
The extra bus on Fridays is a boon for anyone with a late practice.

confused.note: A boon is a benefit; a bane is a source of harm.

questions.passage: The new bridge has been a ______ to the island's shopkeepers. Visitors who once had to wait for a twice-daily ferry can now drive across in ten minutes, and sales have doubled.
questions.explanation: Doubled sales show the bridge has been a great benefit.

distractors.why: A bane is a source of harm, the opposite of what the bridge brought.
A synthesis is a combination, which does not fit.
A respite is a short rest, which is not what doubled sales represent.

definition: stopping and starting again; not continuous

examples.text: The geyser's intermittent eruptions come about once an hour.
Intermittent fighting along the border continued for a decade.
The Wi-Fi in the library is intermittent at best.

confused.note: Intermittent means off and on; interminable means seeming endless.

questions.passage: The signal from the spacecraft was ______. For a few seconds the data would arrive clearly; then the receiver would fall silent for minutes at a time before the stream resumed.
questions.explanation: A signal that comes, stops, and resumes is not continuous.

distractors.why: Interminable means endless; it resembles the right word but means nearly the opposite here.
Manifest means obvious, which does not describe a signal that keeps cutting out.
Circuitous means roundabout, which does not fit.
